title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
text: ggsynteny provides tools creating publication-quality synteny plots comparative genomics. vignette demonstrates basic usage package.

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Install from GitHub devtools::install_github("yourusername/ggsynteny") library(ggsynteny) library(ggplot2) #> Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.5.2

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
text: Let’s start bundled example data showing synteny Arabidopsis, Grape, Rice: data contains two data frames: - chromosomes: chromosome sizes species - blocks: syntenic block coordinates
code: # Load example data syn <- example_synteny_data()  # Inspect structure str(syn) #> List of 2 #>  $ chromosomes: tibble [27 × 3] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame) #>   ..$ species: chr [1:27] "Arabidopsis" "Arabidopsis" "Arabidopsis" "Arabidopsis" ... #>   ..$ chr    : chr [1:27] "1" "2" "3" "4" ... #>   ..$ size   : num [1:27] 30.4 19.7 23.5 18.6 26.9 23 18.8 19.3 24 25 ... #>  $ blocks     : tibble [27 × 8] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame) #>   ..$ species1: chr [1:27] "Arabidopsis" "Arabidopsis" "Arabidopsis" "Arabidopsis" ... #>   ..$ chr1    : chr [1:27] "1" "1" "2" "2" ... #>   ..$ start1  : num [1:27] 2 14 1 12 3 16 2 11 3 16 ... #>   ..$ end1    : num [1:27] 12 25 10 18 15 22 10 17 14 24 ... #>   ..$ species2: chr [1:27] "Grape" "Grape" "Grape" "Grape" ... #>   ..$ chr2    : chr [1:27] "1" "3" "5" "2" ... #>   ..$ start2  : num [1:27] 3 2 5 3 4 2 5 3 3 2 ... #>   ..$ end2    : num [1:27] 14 13 16 10 16 10 14 10 15 12 ...

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Define species order (top to bottom) sp_order <- c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice")  # Create plot p1 <- plot_synteny(syn,                    species_order = sp_order,                    title = "Plant Genome Synteny") print(p1)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
text: Every palette argument accepts, name, 32 palettes ltc package (vendored, ltc need installed). One palette can drive whole plot:  List syn_palettes(); names match case-insensitively ignore spaces, underscores, dashes:
code: p_pal <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order, palette = "casa_natal") print(p_pal) names(syn_palettes()) #>  [1] "paloma"     "maya"       "dora"       "ploen"      "olga"       #>  [6] "mterese"    "gaby"       "franscoise" "fernande"   "sylvie"     #> [11] "expevo"     "minou"      "kiss"       "hat"        "reading"    #> [16] "alger"      "trio1"      "trio2"      "trio3"      "trio4"      #> [21] "heatmap0"   "pantone23"  "remains"    "midnight"   "lincoln"    #> [26] "luminaries" "seafarer"   "shuggie"    "heatmap1"   "heatmap2"   #> [31] "heatmap3"   "casa_natal"

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: p2 <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order,                    chr_fill = "per_species",                    chr_palette = c(                      "Arabidopsis" = "#B8D4E3",                      "Grape"       = "#C5B4E3",                      "Rice"        = "#B8E3C5"                    ),                    ribbon_fill = "uniform",                    ribbon_palette = "#50B88E",                    ribbon_alpha = 0.25,                    title = "Custom Species Colors") print(p2)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Define color palette for chromosomes 1-12 chr_pal <- c("1"="#1B3A8C", "2"="#3B7DD8", "3"="#00BCD4", "4"="#4CAF50",              "5"="#8BC34A", "6"="#CDDC39", "7"="#9C27B0", "8"="#E91E63",              "9"="#FF5722", "10"="#FF9800", "11"="#795548", "12"="#F44336")  p3 <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order,                    chr_fill = "per_chr",                    chr_palette = chr_pal,                    ribbon_fill = "source_chr",                    ribbon_palette = chr_pal,                    title = "Per-Chromosome Coloring") print(p3)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: p4 <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order,                    chr_fill = "uniform",                    chr_palette = "#E8E4DF",                    ribbon_fill = "species_pair",                    ribbon_palette = c(                      "Arabidopsis_Grape" = "#3A6EA5",                      "Grape_Rice"        = "#E8573A"                    ),                    title = "Species-Pair Ribbon Colors") print(p4)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
text: Micro-synteny plots show gene-level conservation: data contains: - features: gene coordinates, strand, names - links: homology relationships identity scores
code: # Load microsynteny example micro <- demo_microsynteny_data()  # Inspect structure str(micro) #> List of 2 #>  $ features:'data.frame':    16 obs. of  7 variables: #>   ..$ bin_id : chr [1:16] "ZONMW-30" "ZONMW-30" "ZONMW-30" "ZONMW-30" ... #>   ..$ seq_id : chr [1:16] "4" "4" "4" "4" ... #>   ..$ start  : num [1:16] 0 444 1333 2325 3991 ... #>   ..$ end    : num [1:16] 443 1340 2325 3491 4242 ... #>   ..$ strand : chr [1:16] "+" "+" "+" "+" ... #>   ..$ feat_id: chr [1:16] "moaE_30" "moaC2_30" "moaA_30" "moeA_30" ... #>   ..$ name   : chr [1:16] "moaE" "moaC2" "moaA" "moeA" ... #>  $ links   :'data.frame':    11 obs. of  3 variables: #>   ..$ feat_id_a: chr [1:11] "moaE_30" "moaC2_30" "moaC2_30" "moaA_30" ... #>   ..$ feat_id_b: chr [1:11] "moaE_10" "moaC2_20" "moaC2_10" "moaA_20" ... #>   ..$ identity : num [1:11] 95.2 88.4 91 93.1 89.7 78.3 82.1 71.5 94.3 90.2 ...

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: p5 <- plot_microsynteny(micro$features,                         micro$links,                         bin_order = c("ZONMW-30", "ZONMW-20", "ZONMW-10"),                         gene_fill = "per_name",                         ribbon_fill = "identity",                         title = "Micro-synteny: moa/moe Cluster") print(p5)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Define custom gene colors gene_pal <- c(   moaE   = "#E06C75",   moaC2  = "#61AFEF",   moaA   = "#98C379",   moeA   = "#E5C07B",   mobA   = "#C678DD",   spacer = "#DDDDDD" )  p6 <- plot_microsynteny(micro$features,                         micro$links,                         bin_order = c("ZONMW-30", "ZONMW-20", "ZONMW-10"),                         gene_fill = "per_name",                         gene_palette = gene_pal,                         ribbon_fill = "identity",                         ribbon_alpha = 0.40,                         title = "Custom Gene Colors") print(p6)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Read your own TSV files syn <- read_synteny_tsv("my_chromosomes.tsv", "my_blocks.tsv") p <- plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("SpeciesA", "SpeciesB", "SpeciesC"))

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Parse MCScanX output syn <- read_mcscanx("output.collinearity", "output.gff") p <- plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("Species1", "Species2"))

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Parse GENESPACE output syn <- read_genespace("synHits.tsv") p <- plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("genome1", "genome2", "genome3"))

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
code: # Save as high-resolution PNG ggsave("synteny.png", p1, width = 20, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")  # Save as PDF for publications ggsave("synteny.pdf", p1, width = 20, height = 10)  # Save as SVG for editing in Inkscape/Illustrator ggsave("synteny.svg", p1, width = 20, height = 10)

title: Getting Started with ggsynteny
text: Since ggsynteny returns ggplot2 objects, can customize :
code: p7 <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order,                    chr_fill = "per_species",                    ribbon_fill = "source_chr") +   theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)) +   labs(caption = "Data source: Example synteny data")  print(p7)

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
text: Publication-quality synteny plots ggplot2 📖 Website & full documentation: https://loukesio.github.io/ggsynteny/ ggsynteny draws comparative-genomics figures pure ggplot2: macro-synteny (chromosome-level ribbons across number species) micro-synteny (gene-level arrows connected homology ribbons). ships parsers MCScanX, GENESPACE, plain TSV input, every colour argument accepts 32 palettes ltc package name — palette = "casa_natal" just works.

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
code: # with remotes (lightweight) install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("loukesio/ggsynteny")  # ...or with devtools devtools::install_github("loukesio/ggsynteny")  # and load it library(ggsynteny)

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
text: Three plant genomes, one bundled dataset, one ltc palette driving whole figure — chromosomes coloured per species, ribbons source chromosome:  Every function follows pattern: , arguments matter (defaults), worked example.
code: library(ggsynteny)  syn <- example_synteny_data()   # Arabidopsis, Grape, Rice  plot_synteny(syn,              species_order = c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice"),              palette = "casa_natal")

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
text: ’s : stacking species tiers chromosomes connecting syntenic blocks curved ribbons. Takes list chromosomes blocks data frames (see input formats ). colours get soft per-species pastels auto-generated ribbon hues:  chr_fill = "per_chr" colours chromosome label separately — minou palette (interpolated chromosomes colours):  quiet chromosomes one ribbon colour per species pair, trio1:  Named vectors keep working explicit mappings whenever need full control:
code: plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice")) plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice"),              chr_fill = "per_chr", palette = "minou") plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice"),              chr_fill = "uniform",       chr_palette = "#E8E4DF",              ribbon_fill = "species_pair", ribbon_palette = "trio1",              ribbon_alpha = 0.35) plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice"),              chr_fill = "per_species",              chr_palette = c("Arabidopsis" = "#B8D4E3",                              "Grape"       = "#C5B4E3",                              "Rice"        = "#B8E3C5"))

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
text: ’s : drawing individual genes strand-aware arrows connecting homologous genes ribbons — classic gene-cluster figure.  ribbon_fill = "identity" ribbon colour encodes percent identity. default light--dark blue ramp; name ordered palette (heatmap0–heatmap3) restyle :
code: micro <- demo_microsynteny_data()   # a moa/moe gene cluster, three strains  plot_microsynteny(micro$features, micro$links,                   bin_order = c("ZONMW-30", "ZONMW-20", "ZONMW-10"),                   palette = "casa_natal") plot_microsynteny(micro$features, micro$links,                   bin_order = c("ZONMW-30", "ZONMW-20", "ZONMW-10"),                   gene_fill = "per_name",  gene_palette = "casa_natal",                   ribbon_fill = "identity", ribbon_palette = "heatmap0")

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
text: ’s : every palette argument accepts, name, 32 palettes ltc package (vendored — ltc need installed; curated use fills white background, dropping pure-black near-white entries). Names match case-insensitively ignore spaces, underscores dashes, "casa_natal", "Casa Natal" "casanatal" palette. "Okabe-Ito", colour vector, grDevices::hcl.colors() names work . syn_palettes() returns named list:  heatmap0–heatmap3 palettes ordered ramps (always interpolated end--end) — natural choice ribbon_fill = "identity"; rest qualitative sets species, chromosomes, genes.
code: names(syn_palettes())      # all 32 names syn_palettes()$casa_natal  # the hex colours of one palette

title: Publication-Quality Synteny Plots with ggplot2
text: Two independent knobs control saved PNG: width/height pixels decide big (sharp) image ; dpi decides big letters relative plot. Letters small → raise dpi; labels overlapping → lower .
code: p <- plot_synteny(syn, species_order = c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice"),                   palette = "casa_natal")  ggsave("synteny.png", p, width = 2600, height = 1500, units = "px",        dpi = 300, bg = "white")   # bg = "white": otherwise the PNG is transparent  ggsave("synteny.pdf", p, width = 12, height = 7)   # vector, for journals

title: Plot macro-synteny across multiple species — plot_synteny
text: Chromosome Coloring (chr_fill): "per_species" — one color per species. chr_palette = "casa_natal" c("Human" = "#4477AA", ...) "uniform" — chromosomes color. chr_palette = "#E8E4DF" "per_chr" — one color per chromosome label. chr_palette = "casa_natal" c("1" = "#4477AA", ...) "custom" — full control. chr_palette named vector "species__chr" keys Ribbon Coloring (ribbon_fill): "source_chr" — colored source (top) chromosome "target_chr" — colored target (bottom) chromosome "species_pair" — one color per tier gap. ribbon_palette = c("At_Vv" = "#3A6EA5", ...) "uniform" — color. ribbon_palette = "#6688AA" "custom" — per-block. ribbon_palette = vector colors Wherever palette expected, single unnamed string first matched built-palette names (case-insensitively, ignoring spaces, underscores dashes) — "casa_natal", "Casa Natal" "casanatal" find palette. Named vectors used explicit key--color mappings, exactly .

title: Plot macro-synteny across multiple species — plot_synteny
code: # Load example data syn <- example_synteny_data() sp_order <- c("Arabidopsis", "Grape", "Rice")  # Default: per-species chromosomes + source-chr ribbons p <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order)  # One ltc palette for the whole plot p <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order, palette = "casa_natal")  # Custom colors p <- plot_synteny(syn, sp_order,                   chr_fill = "uniform",                   chr_palette = "#E8E4DF",                   ribbon_fill = "species_pair",                   ribbon_palette = c("Arabidopsis_Grape" = "#3A6EA5",                                      "Grape_Rice" = "#E8573A"))

title: ggsynteny 0.2.0
text: New palette argument plot_synteny() plot_microsynteny(): 32 palettes ltc package now work name, e.g. palette = "casa_natal" (vendored — ltc need installed). Names match case-insensitively ignore spaces, underscores, dashes. "Okabe-Ito", colour vectors, hcl.colors() names accepted . New syn_palettes() lists built-palettes. chr_palette, ribbon_palette, gene_palette also accept palette names; named vectors keep working explicit key--colour mappings. ribbon_fill = "identity", named ordered palette (e.g. "heatmap0") used identity colour ramp. plot_synteny() plot_microsynteny() now validate *_fill arguments error early typos instead silently falling back. Chromosome ordering longer emits NA warnings non-numeric chromosome names (numeric labels still sort numerically). read_synteny_tsv() longer truncates decimal chromosome sizes block coordinates (previously parsed integers) reads exactly documented eight block columns. Ribbons, chromosomes, gene arrows drawn single ggplot2 layer instead one layer per polygon — much faster large datasets.
